title: North: the Big Dipper and the pole
blurb: Start with the stars that never set from mid-northern latitudes. The Big Dipper points to Polaris, and Polaris points north.

title: Winter: Orion's neighbourhood
blurb: Orion is the easiest constellation in the sky. Use his belt to find the brightest star of all and the winter circle of bright stars around him.

title: Spring: follow the arc
blurb: The Dipper's handle arcs to Arcturus and speeds on to Spica, while its bowl leaks onto Leo.

title: Summer: the triangle and the scorpion
blurb: Three bright stars from three constellations make the Summer Triangle. Low in the south, red Antares marks the heart of Scorpius.

title: Autumn: the Great Square
blurb: A big empty square of four stars anchors the autumn sky and completes your first trip around the year.

title: Around the pole
blurb: The fainter figures that circle Polaris all year.

title: Winter: filling in the hexagon
blurb: The charioteer, the little dog, the hare, the unicorn and the hero.

title: Winter: the southern river
blurb: Faint figures below Orion that reward a dark southern horizon.

title: Spring: the water snake
blurb: The longest constellation and the small figures riding on its back.

title: Spring: the realm of galaxies
blurb: Between Leo and Boötes, away from the Milky Way, you look out of our galaxy into deep space.

title: Summer: toward the galactic centre
blurb: Hercules, the serpent bearer and the teapot of Sagittarius, where the Milky Way is richest.

title: Summer: small figures of the triangle
blurb: The arrow, the dolphin, the fox and their neighbours.

title: Autumn: the royal family
blurb: Andromeda and the constellations around the Great Square.

title: Autumn: the celestial sea
blurb: A dim, watery region with one bright star, Fomalhaut.

title: Far south: the Cross and the Centaur
blurb: The showpieces of the southern sky, never seen from New York. Travel south, or learn them here first.

title: Far south: the southern birds
blurb: Figures invented by Dutch navigators in the 1590s.

title: Far south: around the altar
blurb: An ancient altar and its modern neighbours.

title: Far south: Lacaille's workshop
blurb: Faint constellations named for scientific instruments in the 1750s, down to the south celestial pole.
